summary_paragraph: A 36-week pregnant patient with a history of bipolar disorder and recent bereavement was admitted for recurrent severe depression and akathisia, with plans to resume electroconvulsive therapy (ECT). She was found to have hypothyroidism, which was treated with levothyroxine. She received multiple ECT sessions with good psychiatric response. During her stay, she developed gestational hypertension and preeclampsia, prompting induction of labor at 36 weeks. She delivered vaginally, required manual extraction of a retained placenta, and had a minor vaginal laceration repaired. Postpartum, she developed mild chorioamnionitis, treated with antibiotics. Her mood stabilized on quetiapine, and she was discharged home in stable condition with outpatient psychiatric follow-up and a plan for continued ECT as needed.
